svg.text: Layers 1–2 expanded — how bytes on S3 become arrays in Python · companion to the main ecosystem diagram

g.text: User calls xarray or a reader → calls flow downward through the stack → bytes at the bottom. Each lane is a distinct architectural role.
how you find the data before touching bytes
the API surface and data structures user code touches directly
label reader output with dims/coords/attrs; wrap in containers
green = xarray family · white = non-xarray geospatial containers · also: raster_tools Raster, ODC GeoBox (metadata-only)
what a DataArray/Dataset actually holds · single-process vs parallel/chunked
chunked backends dispatch through xarray's ChunkManager interface (see prose)
bytes → numpy arrays · the sync/async split is the cloud-native battle line
invoked by readers during byte-range decode
cloud-agnostic access · the entry point to remote bytes
backends: S3 · GCS · Azure · HTTPS · local · FTP
bytes-to-chunks maps · makes legacy formats look like Zarr
where bytes actually live on object storage
bold outline = cloud-native by design; thin = legacy
Direction: user code at top (lane 1–2) calls down through the stack; bytes on object storage are at the bottom (lane 8).

Lane 2 has three sub-roles — engines (bytes → arrays), containers (what user code holds, xarray + non-xarray), accessors (domain namespaces). A fourth role — ChunkManager plugins — is internal dispatch plumbing and isn't drawn (see prose).
Lane 3 splits single-process arrays (NumPy, CuPy, Sparse, pyarrow) from parallel / chunked arrays (Dask, Cubed). Xarray's ChunkManager interface is the bridge between containers and chunked backends.
Sync/async split in lane 4 is the cloud-native battle line. Async readers pipeline byte-range GETs; central to lazycogs, async-tiff, h5coro.
Lane 7 (virtualization) is the newer role: reference/manifest files indexing chunk byte ranges inside legacy formats.
Main ecosystem diagram's Layer 1 & 2 collapse lanes 1–8 above; this companion expands them.
